gloss: to look back at; to get even with

definitions.gloss: to look back at, to glance back
definitions.explanation: To turn around and look at someone or something, or to look at something again to review it.

definitions.gloss: to get even with, to prove someone wrong, to show them
definitions.explanation: To succeed and prove wrong those who doubted or looked down on you. A highly motivational usage implying vindication through achievement.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{振|ふ}り{向|む}いて{見返|みかえ}した。
examples.english: She turned around and looked back.

examples.japanese: メモを{見返|みかえ}して{間違|まちが}いに{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: I looked over my notes again and noticed a mistake.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{写真|しゃしん}を{見返|みかえ}すと、{懐|なつ}かしい{気持|きも}ちになる。
examples.english: Looking back at old photos makes me feel nostalgic.

examples.japanese: いつか{見返|みかえ}してやる。
バカにした{人|ひと}たちを{見返|みかえ}したい。
examples.english: I want to prove wrong the people who made fun of me.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}して{成功|せいこう}し、{周|まわ}りを{見返|みかえ}した。
examples.english: I worked hard, succeeded, and proved everyone wrong.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 2 (to get even / prove someone wrong) is very common in motivational contexts. The pattern 〜を{見返|みかえ}してやる expresses determination to succeed and vindicate oneself. The てやる ending adds a combative or defiant tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見返|みかえ}してやる: I'll show them (determined)
- {周|まわ}りを{見返|みかえ}す: to prove everyone around you wrong
- メモを{見返|みかえ}す: to review one's notes
- {過去|かこ}を{見返|みかえ}す: to look back on the past
- {写真|しゃしん}を{見返|みかえ}す: to look back through photos
